channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: JANUS: A Lightweight Framework for Jailbreaking Text-to-Image Models via Distribution Optimization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes JANUS, a lightweight black-box framework to jailbreak text-to-image (T2I) models by optimizing a structured prompt distribution.
  • Uses low-dimensional mixing over two semantically anchored prompt distributions to efficiently generate harmful/NSFW content while maintaining desired semantics.
  • Claims improved attack success rate (ASR-8) and higher NSFW-related scoring across open-source and commercial T2I models, outperforming prior jailbreak approaches.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Haolun Zheng', 'Yu He', 'Tailun Chen', 'Shuo Shao', 'Zhixuan Chu', 'Hongbin Zhou', 'Lan Tao', 'Zhan Qin', 'Kui Ren']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'prompt distribution optimization', 'text-to-image safety attacks', 'black-box attacks']

item.title: ConcreTizer: Model Inversion Attack via Occupancy Classification and Dispersion Control for 3D Point Cloud Restoration
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents ConcreTizer, a model inversion attack to reconstruct 3D point cloud scenes from disrupted 3D feature data.
  • Uses voxel occupancy classification (empty vs non-empty) and dispersion-controlled supervision to handle 3D sparsity and voxelization ambiguity.
  • Shows experimentally that the original 3D scenes can be restored across common 3D feature extractors on KITTI and Waymo.
  • Concludes with implications for privacy vulnerabilities and the need for defense strategies.

Paper Type

  • Research Paper

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Youngseok Kim', 'Sunwook Hwang', 'Hyung-Sin Kim', 'Saewoong Bahk']
  • Tags: ['model inversion', 'privacy attack', '3D point clouds', 'voxel occupancy', 'privacy leakage']

item.title: AI Security in the Foundation Model Era: A Comprehensive Survey from a Unified Perspective
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents a unified, closed-loop threat taxonomy capturing bidirectional interactions between data and models in foundation model pipelines.
  • Organizes security threats into four categories: Data→Data, Data→Model, Model→Data, and Model→Model, with examples spanning poisoning, jailbreaks, inversion, membership inference, data extraction, watermark removal, and model extraction.
  • Frames how vulnerabilities propagate across the ML pipeline and aims to support scalable, transferable security strategies.
  • Primarily a survey that synthesizes attack/defense-relevant threat classes rather than proposing a single new defense method.

Paper Type

  • Survey/Comprehensive Survey

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zhenyi Wang', 'Siyu Luan']
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'threat taxonomy', 'foundation models', 'privacy attacks', 'adversarial attacks']

item.title: Efficient Preemptive Robustification with Image Sharpening
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a pre-attack defense (“preemptive robustification”) that applies image sharpening to benign inputs to proactively improve robustness against imperceptible perturbations.
  • Positions sharpening as a surrogate-free, optimization-free, generator-free, and human-interpretable alternative to prior preemptive/robustification methods.
  • Claims substantial robustness gains with low computational overhead, especially under transfer attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jiaming Liang', 'Chi-Man Pun']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-robustness', 'input-purification', 'preemptive-defense', 'image-model-security']

item.title: A Unified Spatial Alignment Framework for Highly Transferable Transformation-Based Attacks on Spatially Structured Tasks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a Spatial Alignment Framework (SAF) to make transformation-based adversarial attacks work reliably on spatially structured tasks like semantic segmentation and object detection.
  • Argues that spatially structured labels must be transformed synchronously with inputs to avoid misalignment and erroneous gradients.
  • Introduces a Spatial Alignment (SA) algorithm as the core mechanism for synchronized label/input transformations.
  • Empirically shows SAF significantly improves attack effectiveness and reports large drops in mIoU/mAP on common benchmarks (Cityscapes, Kvasir-SEG, COCO).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jiaming Liang', 'Chi-Man Pun']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-attacks', 'transformation-based attacks', 'spatially structured tasks', 'semantic segmentation', 'object detection']

item.title: Knowledge-Guided Adversarial Training for Infrared Object Detection via Thermal Radiation Modeling
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Knowledge-Guided Adversarial Training (KGAT) for infrared object detection by embedding infrared physical thermal radiation relations into adversarial training.
  • Uses theoretical modeling based on rank order of gray values across classes and optimizes predictions to satisfy physical consistency constraints.
  • Reports improved robustness to adversarial examples and common corruptions across multiple infrared datasets and several detection models.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Shiji Zhao', 'Shukun Xiong', 'Maoxun Yuan', 'Yao Huang', 'Ranjie Duan', 'Qing Guo', 'Jiansheng Chen', 'Haibin Duan', 'Xingxing Wei']

item.title: Z-Erase: Enabling Concept Erasure in Single-Stream Diffusion Transformers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Z-Erase, a concept erasure method for single-stream text-to-image diffusion transformers.
  • Introduces a Stream Disentangled Concept Erasure Framework to avoid generation collapse from directly applying prior erasure methods.
  • Adds Lagrangian-Guided Adaptive Erasure Modulation to balance erasure strength versus preservation, with convergence analysis.
  • Reports state-of-the-art performance for concept erasure across multiple tasks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Nanxiang Jiang', 'Zhaoxin Fan', 'Baisen Wang', 'Daiheng Gao', 'Junhang Cheng', 'Jifeng Guo', 'Yalan Qin', 'Yeying Jin', 'Hongwei Zheng', 'Faguo Wu', 'Wenjun Wu']

item.title: Generative Adversarial Perturbations with Cross-paradigm Transferability on Localized Crowd Counting
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a cross-paradigm adversarial perturbation framework that attacks localized crowd counting models spanning density-map and point-regression architectures.
  • Uses multi-task loss optimization with targeted suppression for each paradigm (logit suppression for point regression; peak-targeted density suppression for density maps) plus perceptual constraints for imperceptibility.
  • Evaluates attack effectiveness via increased MAE and reports transferability across multiple crowd-counting models.
  • Focuses on adversarial attacks and robustness implications for vision-based crowd localization systems.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Alabi Mehzabin Anisha', 'Guangjing Wang', 'Sriram Chellappan']
  • Tags: ['adversarial examples', 'adversarial attacks', 'transferability', 'computer vision', 'crowd counting']

item.title: DiffuGuard: How Intrinsic Safety is Lost and Found in Diffusion Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes diffusion LLM (dLLM) vulnerabilities to jailbreaks, focusing on intra-step and inter-step dynamics (including greedy remasking bias and denoising-path dependence).
  • Proposes DiffuGuard, a training-free defense combining stochastic annealing remasking with block-level audit and repair using internal representations for risk detection/correction.
  • Shows large reduction in Attack Success Rate across six jailbreak methods while maintaining utility and efficiency on four dLLMs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zherui Li', 'Zheng Nie', 'Zhenhong Zhou', 'Yue Liu', 'Yitong Zhang', 'Yu Cheng', 'Qingsong Wen', 'Kun Wang', 'Yufei Guo', 'Jiaheng Zhang']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'diffusion LLMs', 'defense', 'attack detection', 'remasking']

item.title: LLMs know their vulnerabilities: Uncover Safety Gaps through Natural Distribution Shifts
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a new LLM safety vulnerability where semantically related “natural” benign shifts can bypass safety systems.
  • Introduces ActorBreaker, a multi-turn attack method that leverages actors related to toxic prompts found within pre-training distribution.
  • Evaluates effectiveness against aligned LLMs, showing improved diversity/effectiveness/efficiency over prior attacks.
  • Develops a defense via expanded safety training using a multi-turn dataset generated by ActorBreaker, improving robustness with some utility trade-offs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Qibing Ren', 'Hao Li', 'Dongrui Liu', 'Zhanxu Xie', 'Xiaoya Lu', 'Yu Qiao', 'Lei Sha', 'Junchi Yan', 'Lizhuang Ma', 'Jing Shao']
  • Tags: ['LLM security', 'Safety vulnerabilities', 'Adversarial attacks', 'Robustness training', 'Red teaming']

item.title: SafeMath: Inference-time Safety improves Math Accuracy
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces ToxicGSM, a dataset of math word problems containing harmful/sensitive contextual narratives while keeping the underlying math tasks well-defined.
  • Audits existing LLMs to study trade-offs between safety enforcement and mathematical correctness on harmful-context math prompts.
  • Proposes SafeMath, an inference-time safety alignment technique to reduce harmful outputs without degrading (and sometimes improving) math accuracy.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Sagnik Basu', 'Subhrajit Mitra', 'Aman Juneja', 'Somnath Banerjee', 'Rima Hazra', 'Animesh Mukherjee']

item.title: Prompt Attack Detection with LLM-as-a-Judge and Mixture-of-Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a low-latency prompt-attack detection method using lightweight LLMs as “judges.”
  • Uses structured evaluation steps (intent decomposition, safety-signal verification, harm assessment, self-reflection) to mitigate jailbreak/prompt-injection risks.
  • Evaluates on a curated dataset of real-world benign queries plus adversarial prompts generated via automated red teaming (ART) under distribution shift.
  • Experiments with a Mixture-of-Models setup for judges; finds only modest improvements over a single judge.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hieu Xuan Le', 'Benjamin Goh', 'Quy Anh Tang']
  • Tags: ['prompt injection detection', 'jailbreak detection', 'LLM-as-a-judge', 'guardrails', 'automated red teaming']

item.title: Estimating near-verbatim extraction risk in language models with decoding-constrained beam search
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a method to quantify near-verbatim information extraction risk in language models (privacy/copyright related).
  • Introduces decoding-constrained beam search to estimate near-verbatim extraction risk with much lower computational cost than Monte Carlo sampling.
  • Shows that this approach captures extraction risk missed by standard verbatim-only memorization metrics, including more extractable sequences and larger extraction mass.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['A. Feder Cooper', 'Mark A. Lemley', 'Christopher De Sa', 'Lea Duesterwald', 'Allison Casasola', 'Jamie Hayes', 'Katherine Lee', 'Daniel E. Ho', 'Percy Liang']

item.title: Claudini: Autoresearch Discovers State-of-the-Art Adversarial Attack Algorithms for LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents an autoresearch/agentic pipeline (using Claude Code) that automatically discovers novel white-box adversarial attack algorithms for LLMs.
  • Reports significantly improved performance over 30+ existing jailbreaking and prompt-injection methods, with higher attack success rates on multiple safeguarded models.
  • Demonstrates attack transferability from surrogate models to held-out target models.
  • Releases discovered attacks and evaluation code, framed as automated adversarial red-teaming for LLM safety/security testing.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Alexander Panfilov', 'Peter Romov', 'Igor Shilov', 'Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye', 'Jonas Geiping', 'Maksym Andriushchenko']
  • Tags: ['LLM security', 'Jailbreak attacks', 'Prompt injection', 'Adversarial attack optimization', 'Autoresearch/red teaming']

item.title: Attack Assessment and Augmented Identity Recognition for Human Skeleton Data
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Attack-AAIRS, extending the AAIRS framework with GAN-generated synthetic adversarial samples to assess and improve robustness of a skeleton-based person identification model (HCN-ID).
  • Uses adversarial attack sample distributions learned by a GAN to augment training for “inoculation” against multiple unseen attacks.
  • Evaluates robustness via cross-validation against FGSM, PGD, Gaussian noise, MI-FGSM, and BIM, reporting improved robustness without degrading test accuracy on real data.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Joseph G. Zalameda', 'Megan A. Witherow', 'Alexander M. Glandon', 'Jose Aguilera', 'Khan M. Iftekharuddin']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-attacks', 'adversarial-robustness', 'data-augmentation', 'GAN-based-attack-generation', 'biometrics-skeleton-recognition']

item.title: Uncovering Memorization in Timeseries Imputation models: LBRM Membership Inference and its link to attribute Leakage
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a two-stage privacy attack framework for time series imputation models: membership inference and attribute inference in a black-box setting.
  • Introduces a reference-model-based membership inference method (LBRM) that improves detection accuracy, including against overfitting-robust models.
  • Shows that membership inference effectiveness correlates with the feasibility of attribute inference, achieving substantially higher precision than a general-case baseline.
  • Evaluates on attention-based and autoencoder time-series imputation architectures, comparing training-from-scratch vs fine-tuning with initial weights access.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Faiz Taleb', 'Ivan Gazeau', 'Maryline Laurent']
  • Tags: ['privacy-attacks', 'membership-inference', 'attribute-inference', 'time-series-imputation', 'black-box-attacks']

item.title: Why the Maximum Second Derivative of Activations Matters for Adversarial Robustness
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how activation-function curvature (max second derivative) affects adversarial robustness.
  • Derives theoretical links to the loss Hessian diagonal norm and sharpness of minima.
  • Finds a non-monotonic/U-shaped trade-off where best robustness occurs for moderate curvature values (max|σ''| in ~4–10), across architectures/datasets and adversarial training methods.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yunrui Yu', 'Hang Su', 'Jun Zhu']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'model optimization/curvature', 'theory (loss Hessian)', 'neural network activations']

item.title: PoiCGAN: A Targeted Poisoning Based on Feature-Label Joint Perturbation in Federated Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes PoiCGAN, a targeted poisoning attack for federated learning using feature-label joint perturbation.
  • Generates stealthy poisoned samples and performs automatic label flipping to maintain attack effectiveness while evading anomaly-based defenses.
  • Evaluated on multiple image datasets with high attack success and limited degradation of main-task accuracy.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Mind Your HEARTBEAT! Claw Background Execution Inherently Enables Silent Memory Pollution
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a security vulnerability in Claw-style personal AI agents where untrusted content processed during heartbeat-driven background execution can silently contaminate agent memory.
  • Proposes an Exposure→Memory→Behavior pathway showing how misinformation can affect later user-facing behavior without user awareness.
  • Validates the threat with MissClaw (social-agent replica), finding high rates of short-term influence, durable memory pollution, and cross-session behavioral impact even without prompt injection.
  • Shows that common content (e.g., social misinformation) and routine memory-saving can enable the attack under naturalistic browsing conditions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yechao Zhang', 'Shiqian Zhao', 'Jie Zhang', 'Gelei Deng', 'Jiawen Zhang', 'Xiaogeng Liu', 'Chaowei Xiao', 'Tianwei Zhang']

item.title: DeepXplain: XAI-Guided Autonomous Defense Against Multi-Stage APT Campaigns
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DeepXplain, an explainable DRL framework for stage-aware defense against multi-stage Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) campaigns.
  • Integrates provenance-based graph learning and temporal stage estimation with an XAI pipeline whose signals are incorporated into policy optimization via evidence alignment and confidence-aware reward shaping.
  • Evaluates in a realistic enterprise testbed, reporting improved detection/defense performance and higher explanation confidence and fidelity.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Trung V. Phan', 'Thomas Bauschert']
  • Tags: ['APT defense', 'Reinforcement learning', 'Explainable AI', 'Cybersecurity', 'Stage-aware defense']

item.title: Alignment Whack-a-Mole : Finetuning Activates Verbatim Recall of Copyrighted Books in Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows that finetuning can bypass alignment/safety measures intended to prevent verbatim recall of copyrighted text.
  • Trains models to transform plot summaries into full text, enabling reproduction of a large fraction of held-out copyrighted books (with long verbatim spans).
  • Demonstrates cross-author/generalized memorization: finetuning on one author can trigger verbatim recall from many other authors; patterns align across multiple providers’ models.
  • Concludes that weights retain memorized copyrighted content and that finetuning-induced security failures undermine compliance assumptions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xinyue Liu', 'Niloofar Mireshghallah', 'Jane C. Ginsburg', 'Tuhin Chakrabarty']
  • Tags: ['privacy/memorization', 'model extraction/verbatim recall', 'copyrighted text leakage', 'fine-tuning attacks', 'evaluation/red-teaming']

item.title: Agent Control Protocol: Admission Control for Agent Actions
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Agent Control Protocol (ACP), a cryptographic admission-control layer that validates agent identity, capability scope, delegation chain, policy compliance, and enables transitive revocation before actions execute.
  • Includes deterministic risk evaluation (non-ML), time limits, and cryptographically chained auditing for traceability across organizational boundaries.
  • Reports adversarial evaluation results showing single-agent evasion attempts are largely blocked and isolation is preserved under coordinated multi-agent stress.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Marcelo Fernandez (TraslaIA)']
  • Tags: ['agent security', 'admission control', 'cryptographic authorization', 'risk evaluation', 'red teaming/adversarial testing']

item.title: Mitigating LLM Hallucinations through Domain-Grounded Tiered Retrieval
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a domain-grounded tiered retrieval and verification pipeline to reduce LLM hallucinations.
  • Uses a four-phase LangGraph architecture: intrinsic verification/early-exit, adaptive search routing, refined context filtering, and extrinsic regeneration with claim-level verification.
  • Evaluates on multiple hallucination/factuality benchmarks and reports improved groundedness and win rates over zero-shot baselines.
  • Identifies a remaining failure mode: false-premise overclaiming.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Md. Asraful Haque', 'Aasar Mehdi', 'Maaz Mahboob', 'Tamkeen Fatima']
  • Tags: ['LLM hallucination mitigation', 'RAG', 'verification/groundedness', 'claim-level fact checking']

item.title: AgentDrift: Unsafe Recommendation Drift Under Tool Corruption Hidden by Ranking Metrics in LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies a safety failure mode in tool-augmented LLM agents: recommendation drift caused by corrupted/contaminated tool outputs hidden by standard ranking metrics (e.g., NDCG).
  • Introduces a paired-trajectory evaluation protocol that replays financial dialogues under clean vs contaminated tool-output conditions and analyzes divergence mechanisms (information vs memory channels).
  • Finds high evaluation-blindness: utility/ranking quality can remain near-preserved (~1.0) while risk-inappropriate products appear in most turns (65–93%).
  • Proposes/uses a safety-penalized metric variant (sNDCG) and finds trajectory-level monitoring is needed; agents often do not question tool-data reliability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zekun Wu', 'Adriano Koshiyama', 'Sahan Bulathwela', 'Maria Perez-Ortiz']
  • Tags: ['LLM agents', 'tool/output corruption', 'evaluation metrics', 'safety drift', 'trajectory-level testing']

item.title: Red-Teaming Vision-Language-Action Models via Quality Diversity Prompt Generation for Robust Robot Policies
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Q-DIG, a red-teaming method to generate diverse, task-relevant natural language instructions that induce failures in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robot models.
  • Uses quality diversity techniques with VLMs to find natural and varied adversarial prompt variants that reveal meaningful robustness vulnerabilities.
  • Shows that fine-tuning VLA models on generated failure-inducing instructions improves success rates in simulation and real-world settings, including on unseen instructions.

item.title: OSS-CRS: Liberating AIxCC Cyber Reasoning Systems for Real-World Open-Source Security
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents OSS-CRS, an open, locally deployable framework for running and combining cyber reasoning system (CRS) techniques.
  • Ported the Atlantis CRS and used it to discover 10 previously unknown bugs, including three high-severity ones, across 8 OSS-Fuzz projects.
  • Focus is on using AI-driven cyber reasoning for security vulnerability discovery and confirmation/patching in real-world open-source software.

item.title: HalluJudge: A Reference-Free Hallucination Detection for Context Misalignment in Code Review Automation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes HalluJudge, a reference-free hallucination detection method for LLM-generated code review comments.
  • Evaluates multiple assessment strategies (including structured multi-branch reasoning) to judge grounding/context alignment with the provided code.
  • Conducts large-scale evaluation on enterprise software projects and compares judgments to developer preferences in production.

item.title: Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs via Persona Prompts
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies jailbreak attacks on LLMs specifically using persona prompts to evade safety/defense mechanisms.
  • Proposes a genetic-algorithm method to automatically craft persona prompts that increase jailbreak success.
  • Evaluates across multiple LLMs, showing reduced refusal rates (50–70%) and improved success rates (10–20%) when combined with other attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

item.title: Relationship-Aware Safety Unlearning for Multimodal LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes relationship-aware safety unlearning for multimodal LLMs by explicitly modeling unsafe object-relation-object (O-R-O) tuples.
  • Uses targeted parameter-efficient edits (LoRA) to suppress unsafe relational combinations while preserving benign object marginals and safe neighboring relations.
  • Evaluates with CLIP-based experiments and robustness testing under paraphrase, contextual, and out-of-distribution image attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

item.title: Anti-I2V: Safeguarding your photos from malicious image-to-video generation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Anti-I2V, a defense to prevent malicious image-to-video (I2V) generation from a person’s photo and text prompts.
  • Targets robustness against adversarial image perturbations by applying noise update strategies in both L*a*b* and frequency domains, focusing on salient pixels.
  • Analyzes which denoising layers capture key semantic features and uses this to train objectives that degrade temporal coherence and generation fidelity.
  • Reports state-of-the-art defensive performance across diverse video diffusion models, including Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbones.

Paper Type

item.title: ClawKeeper: Comprehensive Safety Protection for OpenClaw Agents Through Skills, Plugins, and Watchers
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ClawKeeper, a holistic security framework for the OpenClaw autonomous agent runtime.
  • Implements protection across three layers: instruction-level skill policies, runtime plugin hardening/detection/monitoring, and a watcher-based middleware for real-time state verification and intervention (e.g., halting high-risk actions/human confirmation).
  • Targets system-level threats arising from broad tool/file/shell privileges, aiming to prevent data leakage, privilege escalation, and malicious skill execution.
  • Includes qualitative and quantitative evaluations over diverse threat scenarios and releases code.

item.title: Environment-Grounded Multi-Agent Workflow for Autonomous Penetration Testing
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an environment-grounded multi-agent workflow using large language models to automate penetration testing in robotic/ROS environments.
  • Builds a shared graph-based memory capturing observable system state (network topology, communication channels, vulnerabilities, and attempted exploits) for traceable, context-aware execution.
  • Evaluates in a robotics Capture-the-Flag setting (ROS/ROS2) with high reliability, completing challenges in 100% of runs (n=5).

Paper Type

item.title: Uncovering Memorization in Timeseries Imputation models: LBRM Membership Inference and its link to attribute Leakage
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a two-stage privacy attack framework for time series imputation models: membership inference and attribute inference in a black-box setting.
  • Introduces a reference-model-based membership inference method (LBRM) that improves detection accuracy, including against overfitting-robust models.
  • Shows that membership inference effectiveness correlates with the feasibility of attribute inference, achieving substantially higher precision than a general-case baseline.
  • Evaluates on attention-based and autoencoder time-series imputation architectures, comparing training-from-scratch vs fine-tuning with initial weights access.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Invisible Threats from Model Context Protocol: Generating Stealthy Injection Payload via Tree-based Adaptive Search
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes TIP (Tree structured Injection for Payloads), a black-box attack that generates stealthy tool-response manipulation payloads against MCP-enabled tool-using LLM agents.
  • Frames payload generation as a tree-based adaptive search guided by an attacker LLM with coarse-to-fine optimization and path-aware feedback.
  • Conditioning on observable defense signals and adaptive exploration helps TIP succeed even against multiple defense approaches.
  • Reports high attack success (>95% undefended) with fewer queries than prior attacks, and substantial retained effectiveness (>50%) against representative defenses; includes real MCP system evaluation and mitigation discussion.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yulin Shen', 'Xudong Pan', 'Geng Hong', 'Min Yang']
  • Tags: ['prompt-injection', 'tool-augmented agents', 'black-box attacks', 'LLM security defenses-evasion', 'MCP']

item.title: When Understanding Becomes a Risk: Authenticity and Safety Risks in the Emerging Image Generation Paradigm
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes safety risks in multimodal LLM-based image generation, focusing on (1) unsafe/violating content generation and (2) fake image synthesis.
  • Finds MLLMs generate more unsafe images than diffusion models on multiple unsafe-content benchmark datasets, attributed to better semantic understanding of complex prompts.
  • Shows that fake image detectors are less effective on MLLM-generated images; even after retraining, detectors can be bypassed using longer/more descriptive prompts.

item.title: Policy-Guided Threat Hunting: An LLM enabled Framework with Splunk SOC Triage
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an LLM-enabled, agentic threat hunting framework integrated with Splunk SOC workflows for analyzing large volumes of logs.
  • Uses reconstruction-based autoencoders and deep reinforcement learning for triage/anomaly assessment, and an LLM for contextual analysis to recommend block/allow/monitor actions.
  • Evaluates on benchmark and simulated datasets, focusing on identifying suspicious/malicious network traffic and adapting to changing conditions.

item.title: High-Fidelity Face Content Recovery via Tamper-Resilient Versatile Watermarking
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes VeriFi, a tamper-resilient versatile watermarking framework aimed at AIGC/deepfake media provenance and integrity.
  • Introduces semantic latent watermarking to enable high-fidelity face content recovery after severe edits/manipulations.
  • Supports fine-grained localization of manipulations and adds an AIGC attack simulator to test robustness against realistic deepfake pipelines.

item.title: Why the Maximum Second Derivative of Activations Matters for Adversarial Robustness
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how activation-function curvature (max second derivative) affects adversarial robustness.
  • Derives theoretical links to the loss Hessian diagonal norm and sharpness of minima.
  • Finds a non-monotonic/U-shaped trade-off where best robustness occurs for moderate curvature values (max|σ''| in ~4–10), across architectures/datasets and adversarial training methods.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Willful Disobedience: Automatically Detecting Failures in Agentic Traces
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes AgentPex, a tool that automatically evaluates multi-step agentic traces for compliance with rules extracted from prompts and system instructions.
  • Targets procedural failures such as incorrect workflow routing, unsafe tool usage, and violations of prompt-specified requirements that outcome-only benchmarks miss.
  • Evaluates on 424 traces from τ2-bench across multiple customer-service domains, showing improved detection of specification violations.
  • Provides fine-grained diagnostics by model, domain, and metric.

item.title: The Cognitive Firewall:Securing Browser Based AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Via Hybrid Edge Cloud Defense
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes the “Cognitive Firewall,” a hybrid edge-cloud defense to secure browser-based LLM agents against Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI).
  • Uses a three-stage architecture: local visual Sentinel, cloud-based Deep Planner, and a deterministic Guard enforcing execution-time policies.
  • Evaluates on 1,000 adversarial samples, showing large reductions in attack success rate, including strong gains under adaptive evaluation.

Paper Type

  • Research

  • Tags: ['prompt-injection', 'indirect prompt injection', 'LLM agent security', 'execution-time guardrails']

item.title: Prototype Fusion: A Training-Free Multi-Layer Approach to OOD Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a training-free, model-agnostic method for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection using multi-layer internal representations.
  • Aggregates features across successive convolutional blocks, forms class-wise mean embeddings (L2-normalized) as prototypes, and uses cosine similarity to compute an OOD score.
  • Shows improved AUROC and reduced FPR on multiple image classification OOD benchmarks, emphasizing intermediate layers as informative signals.

item.title: PoiCGAN: A Targeted Poisoning Based on Feature-Label Joint Perturbation in Federated Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes PoiCGAN, a targeted poisoning attack for federated learning using feature-label joint perturbation.
  • Generates stealthy poisoned samples and performs automatic label flipping to maintain attack effectiveness while evading anomaly-based defenses.
  • Evaluated on multiple image datasets with high attack success and limited degradation of main-task accuracy.

item.title: Internal Safety Collapse in Frontier Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a failure mode called Internal Safety Collapse (ISC) in frontier LLMs where harmful content is generated continuously while performing otherwise benign tasks.
  • Introduces the TVD (Task, Validator, Data) framework to trigger ISC using domain tasks where harmful output is the only valid completion.
  • Builds ISC-Bench (53 scenarios across 8 professional disciplines) and evaluates across multiple frontier models, including GPT-5.2 and Claude Sonnet 4.5.
  • Reports worst-case safety failure rates averaging 95.3% on jailbreak-related evaluations, claiming ISC exceeds standard jailbreak attacks.

item.title: Mitigating Many-Shot Jailbreaking
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies many-shot jailbreaking (MSJ), an adversarial prompt-based attack that uses long-context in-context “fake assistant” examples to bypass safety training.
  • Evaluates multiple mitigation strategies, including fine-tuning and input sanitization, both individually and in combination.
  • Finds that combined defenses significantly reduce MSJ effectiveness while preserving performance on benign tasks.
  • Proposes incorporating the mitigation into model safety post-training to address the vulnerability.

Paper Type

  • Research

  • Tags: ['prompt-injection/jailbreaking', 'LLM security', 'input sanitization', 'fine-tuning defenses']
